evidence: It takes a minimum of three days to complete and can be walked in either direction.
The directions in this guide take you from the true right of the Waiotukupuna Bridge (SH38), 16 km west of the Aniwaniwa Visitor Centre.
This section starts on the true right of the Waiotukupuna Stream 100 m upstream from the Waiotukupuna Bridge. It is signposted from SH38.
From the shelter there is an easy downhill walk to the end of the track, 200 m west of the Visitor Centre.

evidence: If you wish to see more of the area, there is a detour you can take through the Ruapani wetlands.
Instead of taking the track to Waikareiti Shelter, take a fork to the right, approximately 2 hours 30 minutes to the south of the Sandy Bay Hut.

Past the wetland the track drops down for another 45 minutes to its end, giving good views of Lake Waikaremoana and the Ngamoko Range along the way. At the end of the track turn right to reach the start of the Waikareiti Track on SH38.

doubts: The walk can be done in either direction; the page describes it from Waiotukupuna Bridge. Start F1 (where Manuoha Track meets Waikaremoana Road) taken as the SH38 start. The main end ('end of the track, 200 m west of the Visitor Centre', heading 'Sandy Bay - Āniwaniwa') has no road-end feature; I gave T6 (place Aniwaniwa) from the heading, but the exact track end may differ. F3 (where Ruapani Track meets Waikaremoana Road) is taken as the end of the Ruapani alternative track, after which one turns right along the road to the Waikareiti Track start; the W2 end itself has no ref. The page's wording of where the Ruapani fork is (2 hr 30 min south of Sandy Bay Hut vs 'from the Waikareiti Track junction') is inconsistent. Manuoha Hut is being removed. The Lake Waikareiti Walk link L1 (anchor 'Waikareiti Track') was not used because the text only names its junction and start.
